checks.name: positive-control-4-squash-equivalent-clean-tree
checks.summary: commit ceb3b20 removed all three probe files from the tree. Because git reset/checkout --/stash/commit --amend are forbidden for this task, the probe-adding commits remain reachable from this branch's HEAD pending the coordinator's integration squash, and a raw scan of this branch still reports leaks found: 3 from those historical commits. To measure the integrated result without rewriting this branch, a non-destructive commit was built with `git commit-tree <HEAD^{tree}> -p bae33d6` (identical final tree, parented directly on the pre-task base, no probe commits, no ref/index/working-tree of this worktree touched) and scanned in isolation via --log-opts pointed at that commit sha: no leaks found (223 commits scanned). The same technique pointed at the pre-deletion commit reproduces leaks found: 3 as a sanity check that the method itself detects real findings.

checks.name: secrets-raw-branch
checks.summary: leaks found: 3 on this task branch's raw HEAD, caused entirely by the three probe-adding commits above remaining in history pending the coordinator's squash; see positive-control-4-squash-equivalent-clean-tree for confirmation that the integrated (post-squash) content is clean Root cause identified at integration: gitleaks git scans all refs in the repository, not just HEAD, so the three probe-adding commits remained visible via the still-existing v2-task/V2-042-ledger-digest-allowlist branch/worktree even after the coordinator's squash merge; deleting that branch and worktree resolved it (see secrets-integrated and all-refs-scan-scope).

checks.name: all-refs-scan-scope
checks.summary: gitleaks git scans every ref in the repository, not only the checked-out branch's HEAD, so a gate stays red as long as any branch (even one not merged into v2) carries a probe commit with an unallowlisted secret shape. Measured: with the v2-task/V2-042-ledger-digest-allowlist branch and worktree still present, 374 commits were scanned and leaks found: 3 (the three positive-control probe commits, reachable only from that branch); after deleting the branch and worktree, 365 commits were scanned and no leaks found. Positive controls for this task were therefore verified in isolation with `git commit-tree` + `gitleaks git --log-opts=<sha>` rather than by trusting a raw scan of the task branch, precisely because the raw scan is contaminated by other refs in the same repository.
